Recorded as 1934-02-28, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 6013 itself. Later further-exemption orders recorded as later events: EO 6615 (February 26, 1934) recites that Nuber 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6013, dated February 3, 1933' and further exempts him until February 28, 1935; EO 6974 (February 21, 1935) recites EO 6013 and EO 6615 ('two periods of 1 year each') and further exempts Nuber until March 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
EO 6013 (February 3, 1933, Herbert Hoover). Text and identity: the dossier's original is the Office of the Federal Register's 1974 compilation, Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II, printed page 1415 (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original true), held as the OCR text layer jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_6013.txt; I read it in full. The compilation PDF itself is not materialized in this checkout (releases/source_books holds only a 133-byte pointer), so the printed page image was not viewed and original_pages_confirmed stays false. The OCR is clean in the operative words; the table's 'Name' and 'Department' columns are split by the OCR into separate lists (names, then 'THE WHITE HOUSE', then 'Treasury Department' twice). The registered APP transcription (mirror_transcription) agrees with the granting sentence word for word, prints the second name as 'Jacob L. N uber', and passed the APP page check. Inventory correction: the dossier's machine clause span (characters 0-1517) begins with the text file's provenance header lines, which are not order text, and stops before the department column; the corrected scope EO:6013#corrected-1 covers characters 1003-1632, from 'By virtue' through '[No. 6013 ]'. It exempts Edwin H. Pearson and Jacob L. Nuber, both of the Treasury Department, who reach retirement age during the current month, from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 until February 28, 1934; both names share the one stated end. Identity: number, date, person and end date agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1934-02-28, inclusive. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 6615 (February 26, 1934) recites that Nuber 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6013, dated February 3, 1933' and further exempts him until February 28, 1935; EO 6974 (February 21, 1935) recites EO 6013 and EO 6615 ('two periods of 1 year each') and further exempts Nuber until March 1, 1936. Each recites this order as past history and grants a new period; none revokes or amends this order, so none is this order's end. No later held order names Pearson. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv with retirement wording for the surname; (2) every WPA 1944 numbered-list entry (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname with retirement wording; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts and jobs/*/data for the person's full name within reach of 'retire' or 'exempt'; (4) a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 6013' and list forms ('Orders Nos. ... 6013'). They found, for Nuber, this order and the later orders EO 6615 and EO 6974; for Pearson, only this order. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 through and after this date (EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938, and EO 7842 of March 15, 1938, running to June 1, 1939), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.

savings.reason: Service performed and pay earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects. Any annuity or retirement-credit consequence flows from the retirement statutes, not from the order, and does not keep the order operative: the order commands nothing after its stated date. The later further-exemption orders recorded as later events rest on their own grant under section 204; they recite this order as past history and do not continue it.
